biochem-metab-1:sites.q: Which pathway occurs in BOTH mitochondria and cytoplasm?
biochem-metab-1:sites.e: Heme synthesis, the urea cycle and gluconeogenesis all cross both compartments.

biochem-metab-1:sites.q: Why can a mature red blood cell not perform β-oxidation?
biochem-metab-1:sites.e: Without mitochondria the RBC depends entirely on glycolysis and can only make lactate from pyruvate.

biochem-metab-1:sites.q: A patient has a defect in the first and last enzymes of heme synthesis but normal intermediate steps. Where do those two enzymes act?
biochem-metab-1:sites.e: Heme synthesis starts and ends in mitochondria with the middle steps in cytosol, which is why defects can appear at either compartment.

biochem-metab-1:ratelim.q: The rate-determining enzyme of glycolysis is:
biochem-metab-1:ratelim.e: PFK-1, not hexokinase, is the committed and rate-limiting step.

o: Has no effect on either enzyme
biochem-metab-1:ratelim.e: One molecule flips both directions at once, so glycolysis and gluconeogenesis are never fast together.

biochem-metab-1:ratelim.q: A patient on a high-carbohydrate meal has high insulin. Which change best explains the fall in fatty acid oxidation?
o: Acetyl-CoA carboxylase is inhibited by citrate
biochem-metab-1:ratelim.e: Insulin activates acetyl-CoA carboxylase, raising malonyl-CoA, which blocks fatty acid entry into mitochondria so synthesis and oxidation do not run together.

o: Electron transport in the respiratory chain
Transfer of acyl groups between enzymes
biochem-metab-1:carriers.e: NADH feeds the respiratory chain; NADPH drives biosynthesis and glutathione regeneration.
Also acetyl-CoA carboxylase and propionyl-CoA carboxylase. Biotin carries CO2.

biochem-metab-1:carriers.q: A malnourished man develops confusion, ophthalmoplegia and ataxia. Which group of enzymes is impaired?
biochem-metab-1:carriers.e: Thiamine deficiency impairs pyruvate dehydrogenase, alpha-ketoglutarate dehydrogenase, branched-chain ketoacid dehydrogenase and transketolase.

biochem-metab-1:glyco.q: The net yield of anaerobic glycolysis per glucose is:
biochem-metab-1:glyco.e: Four ATP are made but two are invested in the early steps.
Hexokinase/glucokinase, PFK-1 and pyruvate kinase are the three irreversible steps that gluconeogenesis must bypass.

biochem-metab-1:glyco.q: Arsenic poisoning allows glycolysis to continue but yields no ATP from the glyceraldehyde-3-phosphate step. The reason is that arsenate:
o: Substitutes for phosphate, giving an unstable product
Blocks regeneration of NAD+ from NADH
biochem-metab-1:glyco.e: Arsenate replaces inorganic phosphate, so the high-energy acyl-phosphate never forms and the energy is lost as heat.

o: A higher Km and lower Vmax
A lower Km and lower Vmax
A higher Km and higher Vmax
The same kinetics but different tissue distribution
biochem-metab-1:hkgk.e: Low affinity, high capacity: the liver takes up glucose only when blood glucose is high.
It is the liver and beta-cell isoenzyme, raised after a meal.

biochem-metab-1:hkgk.q: A 19-year-old with mild, stable fasting hyperglycaemia since childhood has a strong autosomal dominant family history and no autoantibodies. A defect in which protein best explains this?
biochem-metab-1:hkgk.e: Glucokinase is the beta-cell glucose sensor; loss-of-function raises the threshold for insulin release, giving MODY rather than type 1 or type 2 diabetes.

biochem-metab-1:glycoreg.q: Citrate inhibits PFK-1 because it signals that:
o: Energy and building blocks are plentiful
biochem-metab-1:glycoreg.e: Citrate spilling out of a full TCA cycle slows glycolysis and promotes fatty acid synthesis.

biochem-metab-1:glycoreg.q: Glucagon raises cAMP and activates protein kinase A in hepatocytes. The effect on the bifunctional PFK-2/FBPase-2 enzyme is to:
biochem-metab-1:glycoreg.e: Phosphorylation switches off the kinase domain and switches on the phosphatase domain, so gluconeogenesis prevails.

biochem-metab-1:glycoreg.q: Which allosteric signal activates PFK-1 during vigorous exercise?
biochem-metab-1:glycoreg.e: A falling energy charge raises AMP, which accelerates glycolysis.

biochem-metab-1:pdh.q: The pyruvate dehydrogenase complex requires all of the following EXCEPT:
biochem-metab-1:pdh.e: Its five cofactors are TPP, lipoic acid, CoA, FAD and NAD+. Biotin belongs to the carboxylases.

biochem-metab-1:pdh.q: Arsenic inhibits lipoic acid. Which other enzyme is therefore also impaired?
biochem-metab-1:pdh.e: It uses the identical set of five cofactors, so the two fail together.

biochem-metab-1:pdh.q: A neonate has severe lactic acidosis, poor feeding and neurological impairment; serum alanine and pyruvate are both raised. Which dietary change is most appropriate?
o: Increase fat and ketogenic amino acids
biochem-metab-1:pdh.e: In pyruvate dehydrogenase deficiency, pyruvate cannot enter the TCA cycle. A ketogenic diet supplies acetyl-CoA downstream of the block; more carbohydrate would worsen the lactate.

biochem-metab-1:pyrfate.q: In the Cori cycle, what travels from muscle to liver?
biochem-metab-1:pyrfate.e: The liver reconverts it to glucose, which returns to muscle.

biochem-metab-1:pyrfate.q: The Cahill (glucose-alanine) cycle carries which additional substance to the liver?
biochem-metab-1:pyrfate.e: Alanine delivers both a carbon skeleton for gluconeogenesis and nitrogen for the urea cycle.

biochem-metab-1:pyrfate.q: Pyruvate carboxylase is activated by acetyl-CoA. Physiologically this means that when acetyl-CoA accumulates, pyruvate is directed towards:
biochem-metab-1:pyrfate.e: A high acetyl-CoA signals that energy needs are met, so carbon is diverted to glucose synthesis instead of being burned.

biochem-metab-1:tca.q: Per acetyl-CoA, one turn of the TCA cycle produces:
Which enzyme belongs to both the TCA cycle and the electron transport chain?
biochem-metab-1:tca.e: It is complex II and the only TCA enzyme embedded in the inner mitochondrial membrane.

biochem-metab-1:tca.q: TCA intermediates are constantly withdrawn for heme and amino acid synthesis. Which reaction best replenishes them?
biochem-metab-1:tca.e: Anaplerotic reactions refill the cycle; pyruvate carboxylase is the main one. The others move carbon within the cycle rather than adding to it.

biochem-metab-1:etc.q: NADH yields more ATP than FADH2 because it:
o: Is oxidised faster by complex III
Carries two more electrons per molecule
Enters before an extra proton-pumping site
Binds directly to the ATP synthase
biochem-metab-1:etc.e: FADH2 enters via complex II and bypasses the first pump.

biochem-metab-1:etc.q: Which complex contains copper and reduces oxygen to water?
biochem-metab-1:etc.e: Cytochrome oxidase. Its copper centres are required for the four-electron reduction of O2.

biochem-metab-1:etc.q: Energy from electron flow is used immediately to:
o: Pump protons across the inner membrane
Phosphorylate ADP directly at each complex
biochem-metab-1:etc.e: The proton gradient is the intermediate; ATP synthase then converts it into ATP.

biochem-metab-1:etcpois.q: Cyanide and carbon monoxide both act at:
biochem-metab-1:etcpois.e: They block cytochrome oxidase, halting electron flow and ATP synthesis together.

o: It inhibits the ATP/ADP translocase instead
It stops electron flow through the chain completely
It blocks complex I selectively and reversibly
It dissipates the gradient, speeding electron flow
biochem-metab-1:etcpois.e: DNP is a lipophilic proton carrier, so oxygen consumption rises but the energy is released as heat rather than ATP.

biochem-metab-1:etcpois.q: A man taking an illicit weight-loss drug presents with temperature 41 C, drenching sweat, tachycardia and a rising lactate; his oxygen consumption is high. Which effect explains his presentation?
biochem-metab-1:etcpois.e: Uncouplers such as 2,4-dinitrophenol let protons leak back, so substrate is burned fast and the energy appears as heat. An inhibitor would lower oxygen consumption instead.

title.th: เคสใหญ่: ชายหนุ่มซึมหลังดื่มหนักและอดอาหาร
title.en: Boss case: Lactic acidosis after a binge and a fast

boss.case: A 24-year-old man is brought in confused after three days of heavy drinking with almost no food. He is tachypnoeic. Glucose 48 mg/dL, lactate 7.2 mmol/L, anion gap 22. He improves after thiamine, then glucose.

qs.q: Thiamine is given before glucose because thiamine pyrophosphate is required by:
o: Glycogen phosphorylase in liver and muscle
Glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase in the HMP shunt
qs.e: Giving glucose first drives pyruvate into a blocked complex, worsening lactic acidosis and risking Wernicke encephalopathy.

qs.q: His lactate is high mainly because pyruvate cannot:
qs.e: With pyruvate dehydrogenase impaired, pyruvate is shunted to lactate to regenerate NAD+.

qs.q: Ethanol metabolism raises the NADH/NAD+ ratio. This worsens hypoglycaemia by inhibiting:
qs.e: A high NADH/NAD+ ratio pushes oxaloacetate to malate and pyruvate to lactate, removing gluconeogenic substrate.

qs.q: Which enzyme is the rate-determining step of the pathway that his liver cannot run?
His glycogen stores are exhausted after three days. Which organ's glycogen could not have supported his blood glucose even when full?
qs.e: Muscle lacks glucose-6-phosphatase, so its glycogen serves only the muscle itself.

qs.q: After recovery, which single deficiency would most closely reproduce his original biochemical picture?
qs.e: Thiamine deficiency impairs the same TPP-dependent dehydrogenases that caused his lactate to rise.
